Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity needs + QBR

Hi Jonas,

Hope you had a good week. We're coming up on our contract renewal in mid-August and want to start the planning loop. Over the past 6 months our peak token consumption has grown ~45% and we expect continued growth as we roll the new assistant to more cohorts.

High-level asks:
- Confirm options for stepped commit vs. fixed annual (we prefer predictability but need burst headroom).
- What different term lengths do you support (12/24/36) and implications on price?
- Schedule a QBR to review usage patterns and align on onboarding for the enhanced throughput.

Can you propose a timeline and owners? I can share an internal forecast if that helps.

Thanks —
Elena
Director of Platform Integrations
Orion Health

Suggested owners:

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity needs + QBR

Quick commercial options to consider (high level):

1) 12-month fixed commit — baseline throughput + add-on burst pool (recommended if you value flexibility).
   - 5% discount vs pay-as-you-go
2) 24-month staircase commit — stepped increases at 6/12 month marks; deeper discount at renewal
   - 12% blended discount if you commit to projected volumes
3) 36-month enterprise term — custom pricing + priority capacity; requires legal review for custom SLOs

We can provide a short spreadsheet with modeled unit economics based on your forecast. If you want a conservative approach, the 24-month staircase gives predictability while keeping burst headroom.

I've attached a quick matrix with pricing bands: pricing-options.xlsx.

Ben
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-options.xlsx (short stub)
